title: The Harmony: a roomy three-bedroom at a busy Old Klang Road junction.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #425 | THE HARMONY, OLD KLANG ROAD
excerpt: A completed mixed development where Old Klang Road, Jalan Puchong and the NPE meet, with a single 1,033 sq ft layout launched at about RM470,000 and rents that cover the numbers.
takeaways: One 1,033 sq ft three-bedroom layout, launched at about RM470,000.
Fully furnished units rent for about RM2,500 to RM3,000, or by the room.
A congested junction with one way out, traffic noise, and plenty of competing units.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: The Harmony sits over a retail podium on leasehold land, with an affordable-housing block on the same site that has its own entrance and no access to The Harmony's facilities. There are 15 units a floor sharing four lifts, off a 2 m wide corridor that is dark because the units are deep. The facility deck has a resort-style pool facing the KL skyline, a well-equipped gym, a shaded play area and furnished function and games rooms.

There is only one layout: a 1,033 sq ft three-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with a 3.54 m wide living and dining area, a long kitchen with room for an L or U shape, a yard, and a storage room off the living area. Units launched at about RM470,000.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project is where Old Klang Road meets Jalan Puchong and the NPE, opposite a police station, with a KTM station and routes to PJ, Bangsar South, Mid Valley, Kuchai Lama and Bukit Jalil. The shop lots in front are mostly offices, so there are few places to eat. A mosque nearby jams the internal road at Friday prayers, and the low-rise neighbourhoods behind are mature.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Empty units now list at about RM500,000 to RM550,000, and an auction unit went for about RM413,000. Fully furnished units rent for about RM2,500 to RM3,000 a month, and a master bedroom alone lets for about RM1,100. Sean says the numbers make sense for investment and for own stay.

pros: The location: three main roads lead almost anywhere, with mature amenities and options for every budget, from kampung to upmarket, within reach.

The design: the mixed development the area needs, separate car parks for shops and residents, the affordable block kept apart, a 2 m corridor, a spacious 1,033 sq ft layout, and well-furnished, well-used facilities.
Value: launched at about RM470,000, which is why it sold out fast, with furnished rents of about RM2,500 to RM3,000.
cons: The micro site: beside the area's heaviest junction, with two ways in but only one way out, which jams on Fridays, and double parking along the internal roads.

Noise and indirect access: traffic, shouting and horns, and no direct turn in or out, so you U-turn both coming home and heading to PJ. The lobby drop-off doubles as a loading bay, though the interiors are well finished.
Competition: many three-bedroom units at around RM500,000 in the area, though the rents still justify the price.

closing: Sean says it would not be his top choice, because every trip home through the congestion feels like a driving test, but the numbers stand up.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this February 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the completed unit, furnished by The Makeover Guys, a furnishing company Sean works with; prices and rents are from property portal listings. An instalment figure in the captions is unclear, so it is left out.
